papers_read.title_as_printed: A dynamic time series inference learning framework for individualized prediction of mild cognitive impairment progression (Xu et al., Expert Systems With Applications 302 (2026) 130576)
Latent diffusion model-based MRI superresolution enhances mild cognitive impairment prognostication and Alzheimer's disease classification (Yoon et al., NeuroImage 296 (2024) 120663)

what_each_reports.P-78: Longitudinal structural-MRI-only 3D DenseNet encoder + Transformer trajectory model predicting 36-month sMCI/pMCI. External Dataset A (ADNI-3 29 + OASIS-3 144, baseline scan): AUC 0.858 (0.803-0.918), ACC 0.827, SEN 0.769, SPE 0.890 (Table 3). Held-out ADNI Dataset B (101 subjects): single timepoint AUC 0.832, ACC 0.763, SEN 0.852; four timepoints ACC 0.907, AUC 0.871 (Table 5). No CSF measure is used anywhere.
what_each_reports.P-84: Diffusion-model super-resolution of ADNI-1 1.5T MRI to 3T*, then an in-house 3D DenseNet Siamese classifier. 36-month c-MCI (n=77) vs s-MCI (n=129): 1.5T ACC 0.578, AUROC 0.553, SEN 0.623; d3T* ACC 0.650, AUROC 0.625, SEN 0.675 (Table 5). No 2D CNN, no 82% sensitivity, no N=156.

quantity_a: Prognostic discrimination (AUC/ACC/SEN) of a longitudinal sMRI trajectory model for 36-month MCI-to-AD conversion, trained on ADNI-1/2/GO with CDR-SB supervision and tested on ADNI-3/OASIS-3 (external) and held-out ADNI.
quantity_b: Prognostic discrimination of a 3D Siamese DenseNet on native 1.5T vs super-resolved ADNI-1 baseline MRI for 36-month c-MCI vs s-MCI; the study's estimand is the gain from super-resolution, not a best-achievable conversion score.
incompatible_if_same: The record's contrast (CSF 77% vs MRI CNN 82% sensitivity) does not exist in either paper. On the numbers the papers do print, both predict 36-month conversion from baseline sMRI in ADNI, and P-78's single-timepoint AUC 0.832 (0.783-0.874) does not overlap P-84's 1.5T AUROC 0.553 (0.485-0.621). But these are two different models, each reporting its own score. Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes (P-78 does not report P-84's pipeline; P-84 makes no claim about achievable conversion accuracy). Under the rule this is not an incompatibility.

gates.dataset_family: partial match: both ADNI (P-78 trains on ADNI-1/2/GO and tests externally on ADNI-3/OASIS-3; P-84 uses ADNI-1 MCI).
gates.validation_tier: mismatch in part: P-78 reports external validation (ADNI-3/OASIS-3) plus held-out ADNI; P-84 reports internal ADNI-1 evaluation only.
gates.modality_family: match between the papers (structural MRI); mismatch against the record, which casts P-78 as a CSF biomarker study.

endpoint_and_metric: compatible endpoint definition in outline (36-month conversion) and metric types, but the sMCI/pMCI construction differs (P-78 uses dynamic augmentation with pMCI defined from any follow-up and sMCI as MCI at all time points; P-84 uses ADNI-1 baseline MCI with a 36-month status), and the classifiers differ.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: no value at or above 0.97; P-78's highest is ACC 0.907 on held-out data with confidence intervals.
independence: Distinct author groups (Chongqing vs Seoul). Both use ADNI-1 subjects, so some MCI participants may overlap; not determinable.
grounds: The record misreads P-78: it is a longitudinal structural-MRI deep learning model and contains no CSF p-tau/Abeta ratio or 77% sensitivity.
The record misreads P-84: its classifier is a 3D Siamese DenseNet on super-resolved MRI, reporting 67.5% (d3T*) or 62.3% (1.5T) sensitivity on 206 MCI patients, not 82% on N=156.
The recorded disagreement (CSF vs MRI) therefore does not exist; what the papers actually print are two different MRI models' own scores, and neither claims an ordering the other refutes.

evidence_quotes.quote: By utilizing structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) data with flexible time intervals, the proposed network quantifies disease severity and predicts progression patterns in MCI patients over a 36-month period.
The single-modality design restricts integration of key biomarkers such as the APOE4 allele and cerebrospinal fluid tau protein
The c-MCI group was defined as patients who proceeded to be diagnosed with AD within 36 months of the MRI scan
The model was further evaluated to confirm whether it could distinguish c-MCI (n = 77) from s-MCI (n = 129).

record_defects: claim_a 'CSF p-tau/Abeta ratio alone achieves 77% sensitivity for pMCI detection': P-78 uses sMRI only and states CSF tau is not integrated; its sensitivity is 0.769 on Dataset A from MRI, not from CSF.
claim_b '2D CNN on brain MRI achieves 82% sensitivity on overlapping cohort (N=156)': P-84's classifier is a 3D Siamese DenseNet; conversion sensitivity is 0.623-0.675 on 206 MCI patients.
resolution_note 'Different modality (CSF biomarker vs structural MRI)': both papers are structural MRI.
registry records P-84 Best_Metric 'not reported'; P-84 does report conversion ACC/AUROC/SEN (Table 5).
Bridging-evidence entries (e.g., 'P-84 reports Improv. over 1.5T') are headline scores, not explanations of a disagreement.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A claim in either paper that a given MRI pipeline's conversion AUC on ADNI MCI is bounded (or exceeds) a value the other's same-pipeline result contradicts. The AUC gap between P-78 (0.83-0.86) and P-84 (0.55-0.63) is a model difference, and would at most be read as documented incommensurability (different classifier, input resolution, label construction), never as a contradiction as the record states it.
